transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Zhou (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (CISO, Helix), Andre Lopez (Head of ML, Helix), Priya Rao (GC, Helix), Daniel Kim (Infra, Helix)

[00:00] Samir: All right everybody thanks for joining - I'm Samir with Redwood, this is Lena our SE. thanks for making time.
[00:12] Maya: Hey thanks, appreciate it. We wanted to run through a security and privacy checklist, especially around prompts and PHI, and confirm the no-training guarantees.
[00:18] Lena: Yeah we can cover that, happy to go deep. Quick agenda - SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency, and then prompt retention/PII handling and no-training. Does that sound right?
[00:30] Maya: Yep.
[00:35] Andre: Also want to understand how prompt logging works for debugging - what is stored and how long it lives, and whether any of it could be used to further train models.
[00:45] Lena: Totally. Quick top-line: for hosted Redwood we persist request logs for operational needs; we provide controls to disable prompt retention or configure retention windows. And for Dedicated/Private customers the default is no training on customer data and we can opt to never persist prompts in the control plane.
[01:05] Priya: Can you point to contractual language? We need explicit "no training" clauses and also confirmation on PHI handling for HIPAA.
[01:15] Samir: Yes, we'll send the standard compliance pack (SOC 2 Type II, ISO summary) and our data processing addendum; we have a clause that prohibits using customer data for model training unless explicitly agreed. I'll email that after the call.
[01:30] Daniel: From infra perspective, we need details on KMS integration for keys and whether we can bring our own key (BYOK) / HSM.
[01:40] Lena: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments. BYOK via KMS or HSM is supported on Private; on Hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS but we can offer dedicated keys in some enterprise contracts. Key rotation policies are standard.
[01:58] Maya: And at-rest encryption?
[02:02] Lena: All persisted data is encrypted at rest using AES-256; in transit is TLS 1.2+; audit logs also encrypted. We can provide whitepapers and the cryptographic modules.
[02:18] Andre: For the pilot we want to capture prompts and outputs for debugging but store them in our VPC. Is there an option to route logs to customer S3 or to a syslog endpoint?
[02:30] Lena: Yes for Dedicated and Private we can either stream audit logs to customer S3, syslog, or SIEM. We can also provide an audit log sample export - it's a JSON/CSV with timestamps, request ids, model variant, token counts, and optional redacted payloads.
[02:50] Maya: What's the retention window by default?
[02:53] Lena: Hosted default is 90 days for operational logs, but we can shorten that. Dedicated can have custom retention; Private you control retention fully.
[03:05] Priya: On PII and PHI: do you have automated redaction or filters? If an end-user enters PHI, how does Redwood handle it?
[03:18] Lena: We have content classifiers and can apply redaction at the ingestion layer; however customers often prefer to do pre-filtering. For HIPAA customers we recommend Private/Dedicated with default disablement of prompt retention and streaming logs to customer storage for any PHI.
[03:34] Andre: If we choose Hosted but want strict controls, can we disable retention per project or per route?
[03:42] Lena: Yes, retention controls are per-project/route. You can set no-retain flag so requests are not stored beyond ephemeral processing. There are tradeoffs (debugging and analytics will be limited).
[03:55] Maya: How do you prove to auditors that data wasn't used for training? Any immutable audit trail?
[04:04] Lena: We maintain signed audit logs and chain-of-custody records for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted we can provide attestations and log exports covering request processing. For contractual customers we provide a clause plus operational evidence - we can share the log samples and the SOC 2 report.
[04:20] Priya: Can we get a sample audit log with PII redacted so legal can review schema?
[04:26] Samir: Lena will send that sample.
[04:28] Lena: I'll attach an example CSV and an explanation of fields.
[04:33] [05:00] Andre: A couple of technical Qs - KV cache and model variants: does the runtime ever leak cached token state across requests? We have multi-tenant concerns.
[05:12] Lena: No, tenant isolation is enforced at the runtime layer; KV cache is scoped to a model-serving instance pinned to the customer or route. In Dedicated/Private it's all isolated; in Hosted multi-tenant instances are isolated logically and we have strict lease policies.
[05:30] Daniel: SSO - we use Okta, want SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC mapping to AWS roles.
[05:38] Samir: We support SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC integrates with SAML groups and you can map to roles. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your IdP directly.
[05:50] Maya: Audit trail detail - we need who/what/where for any admin action: modifications to retention policy, key rotations, and model rollouts. Can audit logs capture admin API calls?
[06:05] Lena: Yes admin operations are logged with actor, timestamp, request id. We can increase retention for admin logs and feed them to your SIEM.
[06:14] Priya: On the 'no-training' point - customers sometimes worry about downstream model improvements. Do you have an internal policy and is it enforced technically or just contractual?
[06:26] Lena: Both. Technically, training pipelines are separate from the inference store; we tag data and access is controlled. Contractually we commit to not using customer data for model training unless there's an opt-in agreement; operationally we enforce isolation and logging to show no data flow into training.
[06:40] Andre: Is there any metadata or usage telemetry that could leak into model telemetry? For example, aggregate prompt patterns used for system-level improvements?
[06:50] Lena: We only use aggregated, anonymized telemetry for improving system reliability (e.g., latency metrics), not content. Any aggregate usage is scrubbed and we don't include prompt payloads in aggregated training.
[07:03] Maya: Do you have ISO 27001?
[07:06] Samir: We have a current ISO summary in our compliance pack and are certified — we'll include the certificate.
[07:12] Daniel: For KMS can we rotate keys monthly? What about zeroing keys after deletion?
[07:18] Lena: You can set rotation to fit your policies. We support key lifecycle management; when a customer-supplied key is retired the data is re-encrypted or inaccessible depending on the flow; we provide guidance on secure deletion.
[07:30] [07:45] Andre: For the pilot benchmark we plan to send ~100k prompts (synthetic and scrubbed PHI examples) to measure latency and cost. We require that these remain within our VPC and that logs are only stored in our S3. Possible?
[07:58] Lena: Yes on Dedicated/Private. For Hosted there's more constraints but we can do dedicated capacity with streaming logs to your S3. We'll need a short runbook to set up the log sink and IAM roles.
[08:12] Priya: A question about subpoenas - if a court order requests logs or content, what is your policy?
[08:21] Samir: We notify customers and follow our data processing agreement and local law; for Private deployments, customer controls responses. We'll provide the DPA language.
[08:30] Maya: Any known incidents or breaches in last 24 months?
[08:34] Samir: No consumer-impacting breaches; we had a non-customer-impacting auth bug two years ago that was remediated; details are in the SOC report.
[08:44] Andre: Can you outline the model variant fallback policy? If a model is degraded can traffic failover to a smaller variant without changing schema?
[08:53] Lena: Yes we support compatible variants; we can configure automatic fallback by route. Those rollouts are logged.
[09:03] [09:35] Maya: Back to data retention: if we set no-retain, does that affect embeddings or vector index creation?
[09:43] Lena: Embeddings and indexes are persisted where you choose; we recommend customer-managed vector stores for sensitive data. If you choose no-retain and do not persist embeddings, the system will not store them.
[09:56] Andre: About model training again - is there a federated learning or telemetry pipeline that samples prompts for research?
[10:05] Lena: No federated learning on customer payloads. Research sampling is only done on opt-in public data or anonymized telemetry, not customer content.
[10:16] Priya: Can you provide the exact DPA clause language now or will you send?
[10:21] Samir: We'll send the DPA with the explicit language and the contract clause that disallows training on customer data.
[10:27] [10:45] Daniel: Are audit logs tamper-evident? Can you support signed logs or blockchain-style immutability?
[10:38] Lena: We support signed logs and append-only export; we can provide HMAC-signed daily digests for Dedicated customers.
[10:48] Maya: For HIPAA, do you sign a BAA?
[10:52] Samir: Yes we sign a BAA for customers that need HIPAA compliance; for those we recommend Private or Dedicated deployments.
[10:59] Andre: One more on RBAC - can we define fine-grained permissions for model deployment and rollout control? We need separation of duties between ML and infra.
[11:08] Lena: Yes roles and granular permissions exist; you can create custom roles via SCIM group mapping.
[11:15] Priya: Regarding data residency, do you have EU-only data regions and are logs stored in-region?
[11:23] Samir: We have regional deployments in NA, EU, and APAC. For EU data residency we can pin your account to EU-only region and ensure logs and backups remain in region.
[11:33] [12:00] Maya: Ok this is helpful. What will you send after the call?
[12:06] Samir: SOC 2 Type II, ISO summary cert, DPA/BAA templates, sample audit log, architecture diagram, and KMS docs.
[12:14] Lena: I'll add a short runbook for streaming logs to S3 and the sample CSV.
[12:20] Andre: For the pilot we'll prepare scrubbed data and representative load; we'll share throughput targets and expected QPS.
[12:30] Priya: Legal will review the DPA and confirm wording.
[12:35] Maya: Any blockers from Redwood side for starting a pilot?
[12:39] Samir: No blockers; we just need the runbook details and IAM roles. We can spin up dedicated capacity for the pilot.
[12:48] [13:00] Lena: Quick note - default Hosted telemetry does collect request metadata (latency, token counts) but not payload for training; payload retention is configurable.
[13:12] Maya: If we choose Hosted with no-retain, will we still get cost/usage metrics?
[13:17] Lena: Yes cost and usage metrics are retained (token counts, routes), but full payloads are omitted if you opt out.
[13:28] Andre: For the benchmarking, can we get per-token latency breakdown and KV cache hit rates?
[13:34] Lena: Yes SE dashboards can provide token-level breakdowns and cache metrics for the pilot.
[13:42] [14:00] Priya: Final question: any plans to ever change the no-training policy? Are there notice periods?
[14:09] Samir: Policy changes would be notified contractually with a notice period; we also never change contractual obligations for existing customers without consent.
[14:20] Maya: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[14:24] Samir: Recap: Samir sends SOC2/ISO/DPA/BAA and pricing; Lena sends architecture, audit log sample, KMS docs, and runbook; Andre prepares pilot prompts and load targets.
[14:36] Maya: Sounds good. Thank you.
[14:40] Priya: Thanks all.
[14:44] Andre: Thanks.
[14:46] Samir: Appreciate the time, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the pilot kickoff.
[14:52] [End of recording]

Notes on transcription quality: some speaker labels may be approximate; there are occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "BYOK" transcribed as "B-Y ok").

Referenced artifacts / links: SOC2 report (link to SOC2.pdf), ISO cert (link to iso-cert.pdf), DPA/BAA template (link to dpa.docx), runbook (link to runbook.md), sample-audit-log.csv

Explicit assurances captured during call:
- Redwood contractual clause: no training on customer data unless opt-in (Samir to deliver DPA text).
- Technical enforcement: separate pipelines and tagged data to prevent training data flow.
- Retention controls: per-route/no-retain flag, Dedicated/Private full control.
- KMS/BYOK supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted has envelope encryption and can offer dedicated keys on request.

End transcript.
